source: Original. Three-set Venn: 70 students, Chess 33, Drama 24, Robotics 34; C and D 11, C and R 14, D and R 8; x in all three; 7 in none. Three-set extension of 3-1CW P8. answer_box_top_frac set by hand to 0.425 (just above the Venn diagram frame at 0.433) so the crop includes part (a); the ruled box itself starts at 0.686.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Complete the three-set Venn diagram (printed on the page, beside the answer box) in terms of x.
parts.tolerance: Accept equivalent expressions (e.g. 33 - 25 + x). Accept numerical values from x = 5 (13, 10, 17, 6, 9, 3, 5, 7) if the student has found x first.
parts.notes: The work is in the printed Venn diagram above the answer box. A1 for x in the centre and 7 outside the circles. A1 for 11 - x, 14 - x, 8 - x in the two-club-only regions. A1A1 for all three one-club-only regions; A1A0 for one or two. Common error: 11, 14, 8 written in the two-club-only regions without subtracting x: A0 for those regions; one-club regions FT within the diagram.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Write down an equation in x and solve it.
parts.notes: M1 for the sum of all eight regions (including the 7) set equal to 70. A1 for 65 + x = 70. A1 for x = 5. Wrong method: two-club totals unsubtracted give 65 - 2x = 70, x = -2.5: M1A0A0.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Number of students who belong to exactly one club.
parts.notes: M1 for 13 + 10 + 17 or (8 + x) + (5 + x) + (12 + x) with their x. A1 for 40.

parts.label: d_i
parts.description: Probability a random student belongs to at least two clubs.
parts.notes: M1 for (6 + 9 + 3 + 5)/70. A1 for 23/70. Wrong method: exactly two, 18/70: M0A0.

parts.label: d_ii
parts.description: Probability a random student belongs to Robotics but not Chess.
parts.notes: M1 for (17 + 3)/70 or (34 - 14)/70. A1 for 2/7. Wrong method: Robotics only, 17/70: M0A0.

source: Original. Dog 58%, cat 35%, neither 24%; 1200 households; second town dog 46%, both 15%, neither 32%. Parallel of 3-1CW P9.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Draw a Venn diagram and find the percentage with both a dog and a cat.
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.17 or 17. Diagram values may be percentages, decimals or counts out of 100.
parts.notes: M1 for 58 + 35 - y + 24 = 100 or 58 + 35 - 76. A1 for 17%. A1 for a Venn diagram with all four regions correct (FT from their both).

parts.label: b_i
parts.description: Probability a household has a cat but not a dog.
parts.notes: A1 for 0.18. Wrong method: 0.35 (all cat owners): A0.

parts.label: b_ii
parts.description: Probability a household has exactly one of the two pets.
parts.notes: M1 for 0.41 + 0.18. A1 for 0.59. Common error: 0.76 (at least one): M0A0.

parts.label: b_iii
parts.description: Probability a household does not have a dog.

parts.label: c
parts.description: Number of the 1200 households with both a dog and a cat.

parts.label: d
parts.description: Second town: dog 46%, both 15%, neither 32%. Probability a household has a cat.
parts.notes: M1 for dog only 46 - 15 = 31. M1 for cat only 100 - 31 - 15 - 32 = 22. A1 for 0.37. Alternative: n(D or C) = 68, 68 = 46 + c - 15 (M1M1), c = 37 (A1). Wrong methods: 0.22 (cat only) M1M1A0; 0.54 (1 - 0.46) M0M0A0.

source: Original (prior learning: systems of linear equations). Smoothies: Mon 12, 9, 6 for 107.10; Tue 8, 14, 5 for 109.10; large = small + 1.50; Wed 15 small, 10 large, m medium for 153.30. 3x3 extension of 2-5PQ P4.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Write down three equations in x, y and z.
parts.tolerance: Accept any equivalent form, e.g. z - x = 1.5.
parts.notes: A1 for each correct equation. Wrong method: x = z + 1.50 (difference reversed): A0 for that equation.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the price of each size of smoothie.
parts.notes: A1 for each correct price. GDC solver expected; no working required.
parts.follow_through: FT from their three equations in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Number of medium smoothies sold on Wednesday.
parts.follow_through: FT from (b) only if their m is a whole number.

source: Original. Surd product (4 + root 3)(a + b root 3) = 14 - 3 root 3; hence quotient; 8^(x+1) = 16^(2x-1); 3^(2x+1) - 28(3^x) + 9 = 0. Style of 2-6Q early finishers (a) P1 and 2-10CW P4-P5.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Find the integers a and b such that (4 + root 3)(a + b root 3) = 14 - 3 root 3.
parts.notes: M1 for expanding to (4a + 3b) + (a + 4b) root 3. M1 for equating parts: 4a + 3b = 14 and a + 4b = -3. A1 for a = 5. A1 for b = -2. Wrong method: root 3 x root 3 = 9 gives non-integers: M0M1A0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Hence write (14 - 3 root 3)/(4 + root 3) in the form p + q root 3.
parts.tolerance: Accept rationalising with the conjugate (4 - root 3): (65 - 26 root 3)/13.
parts.notes: M1 for recognising the quotient equals a + b root 3 from (a), or for multiplying by (4 - root 3)/(4 - root 3). A1 for 5 - 2 root 3.

parts.label: c
parts.notes: M1 for writing both sides as powers of 2 (or of 4 or 16 consistently). M1 for 3x + 3 = 8x - 4. A1 for 7/5. Wrong methods: 8(x + 1) = 16(2x - 1), x = 1: M0M0A0; 3x + 1 = 8x - 1, x = 2/5: M1M0A0.

parts.label: d
parts.tolerance: Accept u values from GDC or quadratic formula.
parts.notes: M1 for 3^(2x+1) = 3u^2. A1 for 3u^2 - 28u + 9 = 0. A1 for u = 1/3 and u = 9. A1 for x = -1. A1 for x = 2. Wrong methods: 3^(2x+1) read as u^2 or u^2 + 3: M0, later marks FT on their quadratic; u values 1/3, 9 given as final x answers: A0A0 for the x values.
